days.title: Define the scarf
days.shortDescription: Choose stitch, width, and finish line.

blocks.content:
Welcome to Day 1! Today we're making the decisions that set up your entire scarf.

## What you'll decide today

- **Stitch pattern** – What texture do you want? Garter stitch (ridged, same on both sides) or stockinette (smooth on one side, bumpy on the other)?
- **Width** – How wide should your scarf be? Measure a scarf you love wearing.
- **Finish line** – What's your target length? Most scarves range from 50" to 72".

blocks.title: Pro tip
blocks.content: Don't overthink it. A simple garter stitch scarf can be stunning, and it lies flat without curling.

items.text: Choose your stitch pattern (garter or stockinette)
Decide on width (measure a scarf you love)
Post your decisions on the hub

blocks.content:
## What to post

Head to the hub and share:
1. Your stitch choice
2. Your target width and length
3. Any questions you have

I'll reply with feedback before Day 2 unlocks.

Today is all about swatching. I know, I know – but trust me, this saves time later.

## Why swatch?

Swatching tells you:
- How many stitches you need for your target width
- Whether you like how the fabric feels
- If your yarn and needles are a good match

blocks.title: Important
blocks.content: Cast on at least 20 stitches and knit at least 20 rows. Smaller swatches lie about gauge.

## How to measure

1. Lay your swatch flat (don't stretch it)
2. Use a ruler to measure 4 inches across the middle
3. Count how many stitches are in that 4 inches
4. Divide by 4 to get your stitches per inch

items.text: Cast on 20+ stitches in your chosen stitch pattern
Bind off loosely and measure your gauge
Feel the fabric – do you like the drape?
Post a photo of your swatch on the hub

blocks.title: If the fabric feels too stiff or too loose
blocks.content: Go up a needle size for looser fabric, or down a size for tighter fabric. It's worth reswatching to get fabric you'll love wearing.
